requirements.original: Templates declared this way are safe to be used in reply and getreply operations, but they shall not be used in call and getcall operations. All out and inout procedure parameters are completely initialized and all in procedure parameters are either unitialized or marked as not relevant using the NotUsedSymbol.
requirements.canonical: A signature template whose `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and whose `in` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol SHALL NOT be used in `call` and `getcall` operations.

ambiguity.issue: Same issue as for the call/getcall variant: unclear whether a template with all parameters completely initialized is also affected. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: A signature template that has uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol `in` parameters SHALL NOT be used in `call` and `getcall` operations.
Any signature template whose `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized SHALL NOT be used in `call` and `getcall` operations.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.3 -- Templates declared this way are safe to be used in reply and getreply operations, but they shall not be used in call and getcall operations. All out and inout procedure parameters are completely initialized and all in procedure parameters are either unitialized or marked as not relevant using the NotUsedSymbol.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: Initialization of templates without parameters is completed at the place of their declaration.
requirements.canonical: The initialization of a template without parameters IS completed at the place of its declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.3 -- NOTE 2: Initialization of templates without parameters is completed at the place of their declaration.

requirements.original: Initialization of parameterized templates is completed at the time of their use.
requirements.canonical: The initialization of a parameterized template IS completed at the time of its use.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.3 -- Initialization of parameterized templates is completed at the time of their use.

requirements.original: Templates can be specified directly at the place they are used.
requirements.canonical: A template MAY be specified directly at the place where it is used.

examples.text: myPCO.receive(charstring:"abcxyz");

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- Templates can be specified directly at the place they are used.

requirements.original: [ Type ":" ] TemplateBody
requirements.canonical: An in-line template IS written as an optional type followed by a colon, followed by a TemplateBody ([ Type ":" ] TemplateBody).

examples.text: myPCO.receive(charstring:"abcxyz");

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- [ Type ":" ] TemplateBody

requirements.original: In-line templates can be defined directly at the place of its use.
requirements.canonical: An in-line template MAY be defined directly at the place of its use.

examples.text: myPCO.receive(charstring:"abcxyz");

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- In-line templates can be defined directly at the place of its use.

requirements.original: In-line templates do not have names, therefore they cannot be referenced or reused.
requirements.canonical: An in-line template CANNOT be referenced or reused.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- In-line templates do not have names, therefore they cannot be referenced or reused.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: For literal in-line templates, the following types may be omitted: integer, float, boolean, bitstring, hexstring, octetstring.
requirements.canonical: For a literal in-line template, the type MAY be omitted if it is integer, float, boolean, bitstring, hexstring or octetstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- NOTE 2: For literal in-line templates, the following types may be omitted: integer, float, boolean, bitstring, hexstring, octetstring.

requirements.original: NOTE 3: Types of constants, parameters and variables of the actual scope are always unambiguous and can hence always be omitted.
requirements.canonical: The type of a constant, parameter or variable of the actual scope IS always unambiguous and therefore MAY always be omitted in an in-line template.

ambiguity.issue: 'parameters' means formal parameters visible in the scope; 'actual scope' is a non-standard term for the current scope.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- NOTE 3: Types of constants, parameters and variables of the actual scope are always unambiguous and can hence always be omitted.

requirements.original: c) In-line templates containing instead of values or inside values matching mechanisms (see clause 15.7) can only be defined in arguments of receiving communication operations (i.e. receive, `trigger`, `check`, `getcall`, `getreply` and `catch`), in arguments of the match and select case operations, in actual template parameters, at the right hand side of assignments (when there is a template variable at the left hand side of the assignment) and in return statements of template returning functions.
requirements.canonical: An in-line template containing matching mechanisms instead of or inside values SHALL only be defined in arguments of receiving communication operations (`receive`, `trigger`, `check`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch`), in arguments of the `match` operation and `select case` statement, in actual template parameters, on the right hand side of assignments to template variables, and in return statements of template returning functions.
requirements.condition: the in-line template contains matching mechanisms

ambiguity.issue: 'select case' is a statement, not an operation; 'can only be defined' is read as a restriction (SHALL only).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- c) In-line templates containing instead of values or inside values matching mechanisms (see clause 15.7) can only be defined in arguments of receiving communication operations (i.e. receive, `trigger`, `check`, `getcall`, `getreply` and `catch`), in arguments of the match and select case operations, in actual template parameters, at the right hand side of assignments (when there is a template variable at the left hand side of the assignment) and in return statements of template returning functions.

requirements.original: In-line templates not containing matching mechanisms can be defined wherever values are allowed.
requirements.canonical: An in-line template not containing matching mechanisms MAY be defined wherever values are allowed.
requirements.condition: the in-line template contains no matching mechanisms
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- In-line templates not containing matching mechanisms can be defined wherever values are allowed.

requirements.original: d) When used in communication operations, the type of the in-line template shall be in the port list over which the template is sent or received.
requirements.canonical: When an in-line template is used in a communication operation, the type of the in-line template SHALL be in the list of types of the port over which the template is sent or received.
requirements.condition: the in-line template is used in a communication operation

improper_terms.proper: message or signature list of the port type

ambiguity.issue: 'port list' means the list of message types/signatures of the port type definition.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- d) When used in communication operations, the type of the in-line template shall be in the port list over which the template is sent or received.

requirements.original: In the case where there is an ambiguity between the listed type and the type of the value provided (e.g. through subtyping) then the type name of the in-line template shall be included in the communication operation.
requirements.canonical: If there is an ambiguity between a type listed in the port type and the type of the value provided (e.g. through subtyping), the type name of the in-line template SHALL be included in the communication operation.
requirements.condition: the type of the provided value is ambiguous with respect to the port's type list

examples.text: myPCO.receive(charstring:"abcxyz");

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- In the case where there is an ambiguity between the listed type and the type of the value provided (e.g. through subtyping) then the type name of the in-line template shall be included in the communication operation.

requirements.original: e) There exist a number of restrictions on the functions used in expressions when specifying templates or template fields; these are specified in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.canonical: A function used in an expression when specifying an in-line template or template field SHALL obey the restrictions specified in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.4 -- e) There exist a number of restrictions on the functions used in expressions when specifying templates or template fields; these are specified in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.original: In cases where small changes are needed to specify a new template, it is possible to specify a modified template.
requirements.canonical: A new template MAY be specified as a modified template of an existing template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- In cases where small changes are needed to specify a new template, it is possible to specify a modified template.

requirements.original: As well as creating explicitly named modified templates, TTCN-3 allows the definition of in-line modified templates.
requirements.canonical: An in-line modified template MAY be defined in addition to explicitly named modified templates.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- As well as creating explicitly named modified templates, TTCN-3 allows the definition of in-line modified templates.

requirements.original: Global or local modified template: template [ TemplateRestriction ] [ @fuzzy ] [ @deterministic ] [ @abstract ] Type TemplateIdentifier ["(" TemplateFormalParList ")"] modifies ( TemplateRef | BaseTemplateBody ) ":=" BaseTemplateBody
requirements.canonical: A global or local modified template IS declared as `template` [TemplateRestriction] [`@fuzzy`] [`@deterministic`] [`@abstract`] Type TemplateIdentifier ["(" TemplateFormalParList ")"] `modifies` (TemplateRef | BaseTemplateBody) ":=" BaseTemplateBody.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- Global or local modified template: template [ TemplateRestriction ] [ @fuzzy ] [ @deterministic ] [ @abstract ] Type TemplateIdentifier ["(" TemplateFormalParList ")"] modifies ( TemplateRef | BaseTemplateBody ) ":=" BaseTemplateBody

requirements.original: In-line modified template: modifies BaseTemplateBody ":=" BaseTemplateBody
requirements.canonical: An in-line modified template IS written as `modifies` BaseTemplateBody ":=" BaseTemplateBody.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- In-line modified template: modifies BaseTemplateBody ":=" BaseTemplateBody

requirements.original: The modifies keyword denotes the parent template from which the new modified template shall be derived.
requirements.canonical: The `modifies` keyword denotes the parent template from which the modified template is derived.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- The modifies keyword denotes the parent template from which the new modified template shall be derived.

requirements.original: This parent template may be either an original template or a modified template or also a matching mechanism.
requirements.canonical: The parent template of a modified template MAY be an original (unmodified) template, a modified template or a matching mechanism.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- This parent template may be either an original template or a modified template or also a matching mechanism.

requirements.original: In case that the BaseTemplateBody on the right hand side of the modified template contains references to variables, these are evaluated before the modification and any uninitialized fields or elements in these variables are treated as unspecified, i.e. as if specified with the not used symbol "-" for the following modification algorithm.
requirements.canonical: If the BaseTemplateBody on the right hand side of a modified template contains references to variables, the variables ARE evaluated before the modification.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- In case that the BaseTemplateBody on the right hand side of the modified template contains references to variables, these are evaluated before the modification and any uninitialized fields or elements in these variables are treated as unspecified, i.e. as if specified with the not used symbol "-" for the following modification algorithm.

requirements.original: In case that the BaseTemplateBody on the right hand side of the modified template contains references to variables, these are evaluated before the modification and any uninitialized fields or elements in these variables are treated as unspecified, i.e. as if specified with the not used symbol "-" for the following modification algorithm.
requirements.canonical: An uninitialized field or element of a variable referenced in the BaseTemplateBody of a modified template IS treated as unspecified, i.e. as if specified with the not used symbol "-".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- In case that the BaseTemplateBody on the right hand side of the modified template contains references to variables, these are evaluated before the modification and any uninitialized fields or elements in these variables are treated as unspecified, i.e. as if specified with the not used symbol "-" for the following modification algorithm.

requirements.original: The modifications occur in a linked fashion, eventually tracing back to the original template:
requirements.canonical: Modifications of a modified template ARE applied in a linked fashion, eventually tracing back to the original template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- The modifications occur in a linked fashion, eventually tracing back to the original template:

requirements.original: a) In case of templates, template fields or list elements of simple types, union and enumerated types, the matching mechanism specified in the modified template is simply replacing its corresponding content in its parent.
requirements.canonical: For templates, template fields and list elements of simple types, union types and enumerated types, the matching mechanism specified in the modified template replaces the corresponding content of the parent template.

ambiguity.issue: 'simple types' is not a defined term; 'basic types' is the glossary term.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- a) In case of templates, template fields or list elements of simple types, union and enumerated types, the matching mechanism specified in the modified template is simply replacing its corresponding content in its parent.

requirements.original: b) For templates, template fields and elements of record and set types, if a record or set field and its corresponding matching mechanism is specified in the modified template, then the specified matching mechanism replaces the one specified in the corresponding field of the parent template.
requirements.canonical: For templates, template fields and elements of record and set types, a field matching mechanism specified in the modified template replaces the matching mechanism of the corresponding field of the parent template.
requirements.condition: the record or set field is specified in the modified template
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- b) For templates, template fields and elements of record and set types, if a record or set field and its corresponding matching mechanism is specified in the modified template, then the specified matching mechanism replaces the one specified in the corresponding field of the parent template.

requirements.original: If a record or set field or its corresponding matching mechanism is – implicitly or explicitly by using the not used symbol "-" left unspecified in the modified template, then the matching mechanism in the corresponding field of the parent template shall be used.
requirements.canonical: If a record or set field is left unspecified in the modified template, implicitly or explicitly by the not used symbol "-", the matching mechanism of the corresponding field of the parent template SHALL be used.
requirements.condition: the field is left unspecified in the modified template
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- If a record or set field or its corresponding matching mechanism is – implicitly or explicitly by using the not used symbol "-" left unspecified in the modified template, then the matching mechanism in the corresponding field of the parent template shall be used.

requirements.original: When the field to be modified is nested within a template field which is a structured field itself, no other field of the structured field is changed apart from the explicitly denoted one(s).
requirements.canonical: When the field to be modified is nested within a structured template field, no other field of that structured field IS changed apart from the explicitly denoted one(s).
requirements.condition: the modified field is nested within a structured field
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- When the field to be modified is nested within a template field which is a structured field itself, no other field of the structured field is changed apart from the explicitly denoted one(s).

requirements.original: c) For templates, template fields and elements of record of and set of types, the above rules specified for records and sets apply with the following deviations:
requirements.canonical: For templates, template fields and elements of record of and set of types, the modification rules for record and set types apply, with the deviations listed for record of and set of types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- c) For templates, template fields and elements of record of and set of types, the above rules specified for records and sets apply with the following deviations:

requirements.original: if the value list notation is used, only the number of elements listed in the modified template is inherited from the parent (i.e. the list is truncated at the last element of the list notation in the modified template);
requirements.canonical: If the value list notation is used in a modified template of record of or set of type, only the number of elements listed in the modified template IS inherited from the parent, i.e. the list is truncated at the last element of the list notation in the modified template.
requirements.condition: value list notation is used for a record of or set of modified template
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- if the value list notation is used, only the number of elements listed in the modified template is inherited from the parent (i.e. the list is truncated at the last element of the list notation in the modified template);

requirements.original: when individual values of a modified template or a modified template field of record of or set of type wished to be changed, and only in these cases, the index assignment notation may also be used, where the left hand side of the assignment is the index of the element to be altered.
requirements.canonical: When individual elements of a modified template or modified template field of record of or set of type are to be changed, the index assignment notation MAY be used, with the index of the element to be altered on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- when individual values of a modified template or a modified template field of record of or set of type wished to be changed, and only in these cases, the index assignment notation may also be used, where the left hand side of the assignment is the index of the element to be altered.

requirements.original: when individual values of a modified template or a modified template field of record of or set of type wished to be changed, and only in these cases, the index assignment notation may also be used, where the left hand side of the assignment is the index of the element to be altered.
requirements.canonical: The index assignment notation in a modified template SHALL only be used when individual elements of a record of or set of template or template field are to be changed.

readings: Index assignment notation SHALL only be used for record of / set of templates or fields in a modified template.
Index assignment notation in a modified template MAY be used for record of / set of; 'only in these cases' merely restates that it changes individual elements and does not prohibit other uses.
ambiguity.issue: 'and only in these cases' may restrict usage to record of/set of types or may refer to modifying individual elements; read as a restriction to record of/set of.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- when individual values of a modified template or a modified template field of record of or set of type wished to be changed, and only in these cases, the index assignment notation may also be used, where the left hand side of the assignment is the index of the element to be altered.

requirements.original: In case of record of and set of types first apply rule (c) to the complete structure (e.g. truncation) than apply further rules for the remaining individual type structure elements (see example 3).
requirements.canonical: For record of and set of types, rule (c) (e.g. truncation) IS applied first to the complete structure, and the further modification rules are then applied to the remaining individual elements.

ambiguity.issue: Typo 'than' for 'then'; 'type structure elements' means the remaining elements of the record of / set of value.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- In case of record of and set of types first apply rule (c) to the complete structure (e.g. truncation) than apply further rules for the remaining individual type structure elements (see example 3).

requirements.original: Formal value or template parameters of modified templates inherit the default value or respectively template of the corresponding parameter of their parent templates only, if this is denoted by the dash (don't change) symbol at the place of the parameters' default value or respectively template.
requirements.canonical: A formal value or template parameter of a modified template inherits the default value or default template of the corresponding parameter of its parent template only if the dash (don't change) symbol is used in place of the default value or default template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- Formal value or template parameters of modified templates inherit the default value or respectively template of the corresponding parameter of their parent templates only, if this is denoted by the dash (don't change) symbol at the place of the parameters' default value or respectively template.

requirements.original: Modified templates may also be restricted. Template restrictions are specified in clause 15.8.
requirements.canonical: A modified template MAY have a template restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- Modified templates may also be restricted. Template restrictions are specified in clause 15.8.

requirements.original: A modified template or fields of a modified record or set template may also be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.
requirements.canonical: A modified template, or a field of a modified record or set template, MAY be declared fuzzy using the `@fuzzy` modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- A modified template or fields of a modified record or set template may also be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.

requirements.original: A modified field with the @fuzzy modifier becomes fuzzy even if it wasn't fuzzy in the base template and will be evaluated for fuzzy fields described in the clause 6.2.1.0.
requirements.canonical: A modified field with the `@fuzzy` modifier becomes fuzzy even if it was not fuzzy in the base template, and IS evaluated as described for fuzzy fields in clause 6.2.1.0.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- A modified field with the @fuzzy modifier becomes fuzzy even if it wasn't fuzzy in the base template and will be evaluated for fuzzy fields described in the clause 6.2.1.0.

requirements.original: A modified field without the @fuzzy modifier that was marked @fuzzy in the base template loses fuzzy evaluation and the template on the right hand side of and assignment shall be evaluated just once when the assignment is evaluated for the first time.
requirements.canonical: A modified field without the `@fuzzy` modifier that was marked `@fuzzy` in the base template loses fuzzy evaluation, and the template on the right hand side of its assignment SHALL be evaluated just once, when the assignment is evaluated for the first time.
requirements.condition: the field was @fuzzy in the base template and is modified without @fuzzy
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- A modified field without the @fuzzy modifier that was marked @fuzzy in the base template loses fuzzy evaluation and the template on the right hand side of and assignment shall be evaluated just once when the assignment is evaluated for the first time.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: If a fuzzy modified template modifies a non-fuzzy unparameterized template, the inherited fields before modification will be the same for every evaluation of the fuzzy template.
requirements.canonical: If a fuzzy modified template modifies a non-fuzzy unparameterized template, the inherited fields before modification ARE the same for every evaluation of the fuzzy template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- NOTE 2: If a fuzzy modified template modifies a non-fuzzy unparameterized template, the inherited fields before modification will be the same for every evaluation of the fuzzy template.

requirements.original: a) A modified template shall not refer to itself, either directly or indirectly, i.e. recursive derivation is not allowed.
requirements.canonical: A modified template SHALL NOT refer to itself, either directly or indirectly (recursive derivation).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- a) A modified template shall not refer to itself, either directly or indirectly, i.e. recursive derivation is not allowed.

requirements.original: b) If a base template has a formal parameter list, the following rules apply to all modified templates derived from that base template, whether or not they are derived in one or several modification steps: 1) the derived template shall not omit parameters and change types or names of parameters defined at any of the modification steps between the base template and the actual modified template;
requirements.canonical: A modified template derived (in one or several steps) from a base template with a formal parameter list SHALL NOT omit parameters defined at any of the modification steps between the base template and the modified template.
requirements.condition: the base template has a formal parameter list
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- b) If a base template has a formal parameter list, the following rules apply to all modified templates derived from that base template, whether or not they are derived in one or several modification steps: 1) the derived template shall not omit parameters and change types or names of parameters defined at any of the modification steps between the base template and the actual modified template;

requirements.original: b) If a base template has a formal parameter list, the following rules apply to all modified templates derived from that base template, whether or not they are derived in one or several modification steps: 1) the derived template shall not omit parameters and change types or names of parameters defined at any of the modification steps between the base template and the actual modified template;
requirements.canonical: A modified template derived from a base template with a formal parameter list SHALL NOT change the types or names of parameters defined at any of the modification steps between the base template and the modified template.
requirements.condition: the base template has a formal parameter list
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- b) If a base template has a formal parameter list, the following rules apply to all modified templates derived from that base template, whether or not they are derived in one or several modification steps: 1) the derived template shall not omit parameters and change types or names of parameters defined at any of the modification steps between the base template and the actual modified template;

requirements.original: b) If a base template has a formal parameter list, the following rules apply to all modified templates derived from that base template, whether or not they are derived in one or several modification steps: 2) a template parameter restriction of a derived template specified at any of the modification steps between the base template and the actual modified template can be changed to a stricter one (see table 13a in clause 15.8);
requirements.canonical: A modified template MAY change the template parameter restriction of a formal parameter specified at any modification step between the base template and the modified template to a stricter one.
requirements.condition: the base template has a formal parameter list
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- b) If a base template has a formal parameter list, the following rules apply to all modified templates derived from that base template, whether or not they are derived in one or several modification steps: 2) a template parameter restriction of a derived template specified at any of the modification steps between the base template and the actual modified template can be changed to a stricter one (see table 13a in clause 15.8);

requirements.original: b) If a base template has a formal parameter list, the following rules apply to all modified templates derived from that base template, whether or not they are derived in one or several modification steps: 3) a derived template can have additional (appended) parameters if wished;
requirements.canonical: A modified template derived from a parameterized base template MAY have additional parameters appended to the formal parameter list.
requirements.condition: the base template has a formal parameter list
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- b) If a base template has a formal parameter list, the following rules apply to all modified templates derived from that base template, whether or not they are derived in one or several modification steps: 3) a derived template can have additional (appended) parameters if wished;

requirements.original: 4) if the dash (don't change) symbol is used at the place of a default value or default template, the corresponding parameter of the parent template shall have a valid default value or default template, either assigned directly or inherited.
requirements.canonical: If the dash (don't change) symbol is used in place of a default value or default template of a formal parameter of a modified template, the corresponding parameter of the parent template SHALL have a valid default value or default template, either assigned directly or inherited.
requirements.condition: the dash symbol is used as default of a modified template parameter
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- 4) if the dash (don't change) symbol is used at the place of a default value or default template, the corresponding parameter of the parent template shall have a valid default value or default template, either assigned directly or inherited.

requirements.original: If not, this shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: If the dash (don't change) symbol is used as default of a modified template parameter and the corresponding parent parameter has no valid default value or default template, this SHALL cause an error.
requirements.condition: the parent parameter has no valid default
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- If not, this shall cause an error.

requirements.original: c) Restrictions on referencing elements of templates or template fields are described in clause 15.6: for modified templates the rules for the left hand side of assignments apply.
requirements.canonical: Referencing elements of templates or template fields in a modified template SHALL follow the rules for the left hand side of assignments given in clause 15.6.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- c) Restrictions on referencing elements of templates or template fields are described in clause 15.6: for modified templates the rules for the left hand side of assignments apply.

requirements.original: d) Limitations on template restrictions described in clause 15.8 shall apply.
requirements.canonical: A modified template SHALL obey the limitations on template restrictions described in clause 15.8.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- d) Limitations on template restrictions described in clause 15.8 shall apply.

requirements.original: e) After completing initialization, modified global and local templates that do not contain the @abstract modifier shall be fully initialized.
requirements.canonical: A global or local modified template without the `@abstract` modifier SHALL be completely initialized after its initialization is completed.
requirements.condition: the modified template has no @abstract modifier
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- e) After completing initialization, modified global and local templates that do not contain the @abstract modifier shall be fully initialized.

requirements.original: f) If the base template has a restriction, the modified template derived from it shall have the same or less strict template restriction (see table 13b in clause 15.8).
requirements.canonical: If the base template has a template restriction, the modified template derived from it SHALL have the same or a less strict template restriction (see table 13b).
requirements.condition: the base template has a template restriction

readings: If the base template has a template restriction, the modified template SHALL have the same or a less strict template restriction (an unrestricted modified template is allowed).
If the base template has a template restriction, the modified template SHALL have the same or a stricter template restriction.
ambiguity.issue: The example 8 comments ('Allowed ... less restrictive') match the first reading, but deriving a less strict template from a restricted one contradicts the usual parameter rule in item b)2) ('stricter'); first reading chosen per the text and example.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- f) If the base template has a restriction, the modified template derived from it shall have the same or less strict template restriction (see table 13b in clause 15.8).

requirements.original: If the base template does not have a template restriction, the modified template derived from it shall not have a template restriction.
requirements.canonical: If the base template does not have a template restriction, the modified template derived from it SHALL NOT have a template restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- If the base template does not have a template restriction, the modified template derived from it shall not have a template restriction.

requirements.original: NOTE 3: Initialization of modified templates without parameters is completed at the place of their declaration.
requirements.canonical: The initialization of a modified template without parameters IS completed at the place of its declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- NOTE 3: Initialization of modified templates without parameters is completed at the place of their declaration.

requirements.original: Initialization of modified parameterized templates is completed at the time of their use.
requirements.canonical: The initialization of a parameterized modified template IS completed at the time of its use.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.5 -- Initialization of modified parameterized templates is completed at the time of their use.
